$comment: The ONLY declaration of platform support. The app, the website and the README all read this file — if they disagree with it, they are wrong. Never add a row here that the code cannot actually deliver.

linux.notes: First-class. OpenRC, runit, s6, dinit and systemd are all detected, never assumed.

windows.notes: Second target. Every check needs a native implementation — none of the Linux probes translate.

macos.notes: Dropped 2026-07-28. Cannot be built, signed or notarised without Apple hardware and a paid developer account.

android.notes: Dropped 2026-07-28. Unrooted Android cannot read firewall state, IPv6 routing or the Wi-Fi MAC, which is most of what Veil checks.

$comment_capability: full = the check works and is trustworthy. partial = it answers a narrower question than on Linux, and the UI must say which. none = the platform does not permit it; show 'Not applicable here', never a failure.

caveats.windows.mac: Windows exposes the adapter's MAC but not a per-network randomisation policy the way NetworkManager does. Veil can report the current MAC and whether Windows' own random-hardware-addresses setting is on; it cannot report per-SSID behaviour.
caveats.windows.fw: Reads Windows Defender Firewall profile state. A third-party firewall replacing it will read as 'applied by something else', not as a failure.
caveats.windows.disk: Reports BitLocker status. An unencrypted machine with a TPM present is still unencrypted — do not soften that.
